source_text: V. Ὁ δὲ θαυμασιώτατος Πολύκαρπος τὸ μὲν πρῶτον ἀκούσας οὐκ ἐταράχθη, ἀλλ᾽ ἐβούλετο κατὰ πόλιν μένειν· οἱ δὲ πλείους ἔπειθον αὐτὸν ὑπεξελθεῖν. Καὶ ὑπεξῆλθεν εἰς ἀγρίδιον οὐ μακρὰν ἀπέχον ἀπὸ τῆς πόλεως, καὶ διέτριβεν μετ᾽ ὀλίγων, νύκτα καὶ ἡμέραν οὐδὲν ἕτερον ποιῶν ἢ προσευχόμενος περὶ πάντων καὶ τῶν κατὰ τὴν οἰκουμένην ἐκκλησιῶν. Ὅπερ ἦν σύνηθες αὐτῷ. Καὶ προσευχόμενος ἐν ὀπτασίᾳ γέγονεν πρὸ τριῶν ἡμερῶν τοῦ συλληφθῆναι αὐτόν, καὶ εἶδεν τὸ προσκεφάλαιον αὐτοῦ ὑπὸ πυρὸς κατακαιόμενον· καὶ στραφεὶς εἶπεν πρὸς τοὺς σὺν αὐτῷ· Δεῖ με ζῶντα καῆναι.
thought_title: Polycarp withdraws, prays, and sees his burning
orientation: After the failed volunteer, the account turns to Polycarp, who withdrew from the city, prayed constantly, and accepted arrest.
pass_a_gloss: But the most marvelous Polycarp at first having heard was not troubled, but wanted to remain in the city; but the many were persuading him to withdraw. And he withdrew into a small country place not far distant from the city, and he spent time with few, night and day doing nothing other except praying concerning all and the churches throughout the inhabited world. Which was customary for him. And while praying he came to be in a vision three days before his being arrested, and he saw his pillow being burned up by fire; and having turned he said to those with him: It is necessary for me living to be burned.

choices.why: superlative degree in source, kept as superlative without adding martyr honor
brief uses withdrew for Polycarp, and verb means go out aside rather than flee in fear
diminutive of field, place outside city, without assuming farmhouse or estate building

choices.english: It is necessary for me living to be burned
choices.why: keeps impersonal necessity and living as separate present participle, not polished idiom

pass_b_english: Polycarp, that most marvelous man, was unshaken when he first heard. He wanted to remain in the city, but most of the others urged him to withdraw. So he withdrew to a small country place not far from the city and stayed there with a few companions, spending night and day in nothing but prayer for everyone and for the churches throughout the world, as was his habit.
Three days before his arrest, while he was at prayer, he entered a vision and saw his pillow consumed by fire. Then he turned to those with him and said, "I must be burned alive."
